md:
I sometimes condition myself for irl eye-contact by randomly pausing videos when people look at the camera (and have their mouths closed) and staring into their eyes. Every once in a while, something about the setting or person makes it a bit hypnotic (my pulse changes and hearing dulls). 

Relatedly, I've also realised that the reason I always wince when streamers "maximise" their cam windows (for instance, at the beginning/end of streams when they turn their screens off) has been that this essentially forces you to make eye-contact with them. A large face (with larger features still) erupts through your screen and invites, or rather, demands, contact between your eyes and its own. You look away and it emits human sounds, forcing your body to instinctively turn back towards the source - which in turn gloatingly smiles at having made you look. Consider the manner in which this face resides upon your screen at other points in time - confined to a small and static webcam window at the corner of your stream, small enough for you to keep track of it through your peripheral vision, and static enough for you to rule out the possibility of sudden, forceful eye-contact.
